items.why: Hand-pulled Lanzhou beef noodles in clear broth from a fully halal shop (BOT tier H), a Hui Muslim classic; it is a soupy noodle dish, so skip it if your stomach is unsettled. Now offered as a dinner swap on 19 and 21 Dec.

items.imageCaption: K.S. Lo Gallery building that houses the tea house
items.dish: Vegetarian dim sum with Chinese tea
items.place: LockCha Tea House, G/F, K.S. Lo Gallery, Hong Kong Park, 10 Cotton Tree Drive, Admiralty
items.costBasis: HKD 150 (120-200): dim sum about HKD 40 a basket plus tea HKD 38-200
items.why: All-vegetarian dim sum and fine Chinese tea in a colonial building in Hong Kong Park, a calm take on Hong Kong yum cha (BOT halal kitchen); steamed and mild.

items.imageCaption: Chrisly Café shopfront at Harbour Pinnacle (OpenRice photo)
items.dish: Hong Kong café breakfast (eggs, toast, milk tea)
items.place: Chrisly Café, Shops G7-G8, G/F, Harbour Pinnacle, 8 Minden Avenue, Tsim Sha Tsui
items.costBasis: HKD 60 (42-70): breakfast sets HKD 42-62 with tea or coffee
items.why: A cha chaan teng-style café, the everyday Hong Kong breakfast of eggs, toast and milk tea; halal unconfirmed because its menu lists ham and char siu despite a BOT listing. Was the breakfast alternative 20 to 23 Dec.

items.imageCaption: Vegetarian dish served at the Po Lin Monastery kitchen
items.place: Po Lin Monastery Vegetarian Kitchen, Ngong Ping, Lantau
items.costBasis: HKD 150 (100-200) for the regular meal ticket
items.why: The monastery's famous vegetarian set meal beside the Big Buddha, a Lantau tradition for decades; mild tofu, mushroom and vegetable dishes, not certified halal.

items.imageCaption: Po Lin snack shop with its tofu pudding sign
items.dish: Tofu pudding and steamed vegetarian snacks
items.place: Po Lin Monastery snack shop, next to the Vegetarian Kitchen (left of the Main Shrine Hall), Ngong Ping, Lantau
items.costBasis: HKD 60 (40-80) for two or three snacks; no price list published
items.why: Quick monastery snacks, best known for the house-made tofu pudding; light and mild, but skip the ice cream, which a reviewer says is not vegetarian.

items.imageCaption: Xinjiang spread: lamb skewers, samsa, naan, polo
items.dish: Xinjiang lamb skewers, big-plate chicken and polo
items.place: Avanti Bistro, 2/F Double Set Commercial Centre, 37A-B Jordan Road, Jordan
items.why: Halal Xinjiang cooking from a BOT halal kitchen in Jordan, the Silk Road side of Chinese food; oily lamb with cumin and chilli, so rough on a careful stomach.

items.imageCaption: Little Sheep Village Hot Pot Buffet entrance
items.dish: Halal lamb and beef hotpot buffet
items.place: Little Sheep Village Hot Pot Buffet, 2/F Full Win Commercial Centre, 573 Nathan Road, Yau Ma Tei
items.why: All-you-can-eat Mongolian-style hotpot from a fully halal chain (BOT tier H); a buffet and a broth meal, so rough on the stomach.

items.imageCaption: Steamed momos with chili dip
items.place: My Kitchen (Tibetan), 180 Shanghai Street, Jordan (BOT list gives G/F, 2H Saigon Street)
items.why: A small fully halal (BOT tier H) Tibetan kitchen in Jordan known for its momos; steamed and mild, but the chilli dip and the thukpa noodle soup are the rougher parts.

items.imageCaption: Uyghur polo (rice pilaf with lamb) at Loulan
items.dish: Uyghur polo (lamb pilaf) and laghman noodles
items.place: Loulan Islam Restaurant, Rua de Cinco de Outubro 169, Macau
items.why: A Uyghur restaurant near Senado Square, pork-free and alcohol-free with halal meat; oily laghman noodles and lamb, so rough on the stomach. Replaced by Aladdin Noodle Workshop two doors away: Loulan's reviews are weak and its halal status is questioned.

items.imageCaption: North Palace dining room at The Londoner
items.dish: Northern Chinese hand-pulled noodles, lamb and dumplings
items.place: North Palace, 1/F The Londoner Macao, Estrada do Istmo, Cotai
items.why: The Londoner's Northern Chinese room, with no pork and all-halal meat on the menu (BOT halal-friendly); dropped because about US$112 for two is poor value for noodles and dumplings.

items.imageCaption: Vegetarian noodle tray from the Grand Lisboa Palace stall
items.place: Vegetarian Farm (田耕閣養生館), GLP Food Hall, Shop 215, Level 2 (East Entrance), Grand Lisboa Palace, Cotai, Macau
items.why: A vegetarian noodle and dumpling stall in the Grand Lisboa Palace food hall, on the BOT list as a halal kitchen; other stalls sell pork, so order only from this one.

items.dish: Hand-pulled beef noodles, stir-fried or in a mild broth
items.place: Macau Halal Aladdin Handmade Noodle Workshop (阿拉丁手工麵坊), Rua de Cinco de Outubro 201, Macau (十月初五日街201號)
items.cuisine: Halal Lanzhou and Xinjiang noodles (hand-pulled beef noodles, stir-fried noodles, lamb skewers, lamb pilaf)
items.costBasis: MOP 70 (50-100) a head: Aladdin handmade beef noodles MOP 40, bamboo-shoot or pickled-cabbage beef noodles MOP 45, stir-fried beef noodles MOP 48, braised beef and potato mixed noodles MOP 52, lamb chop pilaf MOP 78 (menu photo, Nov 2026); Google price band MOP 1-100
items.why: Halal Lanzhou and Xinjiang noodle shop near Senado Square, new and well reviewed; ask to see the halal certificate, and ask for chilli on the side.
items.source: https://www.google.com/maps/search/Macau+Halal+Aladdin+Handmade+Noodle+Workshop (menu photo dated Nov 2026; Google 4.9 from 17 reviews, checked 9 Nov 2026)
